C1.quote: One of my goals for Python was to make it so that all objects were "first class." By this, I meant that I wanted all objects that could be named in the language ... to have equal status.
C1.statement: Every object that can be named has equal, first-class status: assignable, passable, storable, including types themselves.

C2.quote: In Python, variables are simply names that refer to objects. Variables do not need to be declared before they are assigned and they can even change type in the middle of a program.
C2.statement: Variables are names referring to objects, needing no declaration, and all type checking happens at run time.

C3.quote: instead of using braces for statement grouping, it uses indentation
C3.statement: Statements are grouped by indentation rather than by braces or keywords.

C4.quote: I decided that there should be no undefined result values in Python – instead, exceptions should always be raised when no correct return value can be computed.
C4.statement: There are no undefined result values: an exception is always raised when no correct value can be computed, and errors never pass silently.

C5.quote: With explicit references, there is no need to have a special syntax for method definitions nor do you have to worry about complicated semantics concerning variable lookup. Instead, one simply defines a function whose first argument corresponds to the instance, which by convention is named "self."
C5.statement: A method is just a function whose first argument, by convention self, is the instance; explicit reference is the only way to reach instance variables.

C6.quote: making the class object itself callable was the right, "minimal" solution, requiring no new syntax... what I had done was simply to turn each class into its own factory.
C6.statement: Prefer the minimal solution that reuses existing mechanisms over adding new syntax.

C7.quote: Using / 0-based indexing, half-open intervals, and suitable defaults (as Python / ended up having), they are beautiful: a[:n] and a[i:i+n]
C7.statement: Index from 0 with half-open intervals and suitable defaults, so common slices need no +1/-1 corrections.
